sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

content.text:
Case L07: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T1-weighted MRI.

Volume: 206x206x166 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case L07 | sequence T1 | shape (i,j,k)=(206, 206, 166) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: lipomatous soft-tissue tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 83/166 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I can clearly spot the lesion now, a bright fatty mass in the anterior thigh. I'll pull up axial slice 83 with markers and mark a positive point there.

content.thinking:
The orientation here is a bit confusing—I need to figure out which axis corresponds to axial versus sagittal given the slice ranges. Looking at the sagittal view around slice 103 in C3, the green mask appears roughly round.

Checking proportions across the coronal, sagittal, and axial views, the superior-inferior extent of the mask seems roughly consistent once I account for pixel scale and slice count, even though the vertical span looks small in some displays. C1 and C2 appear to be subcutaneous or intermuscular fat rather than lesion, while C3 touches the mask edge with just a small rim overlap.

C4 and C5 also look like intermuscular fat and I'm leaning toward rejecting them. C3 is trickier though -- there's a sliver near the anterior-left tip and posterior region where the magenta extends beyond the green mask boundary, possibly indicating lesion periphery or just adjacent fat around vessels, so I want to look more carefully at the mask outline on the sagittal view before deciding.

Since the sagittal view is cropped tightly to the mask, I can't assess the superior/inferior extent this way, so I should switch to a coronal sheet to better judge those boundaries.

I want to check the full slice to see what's actually there beyond the crop.

content.text: axial 128/166 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 9/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm tracing the bright lesion at axial 128, noting it extends toward the femur with a grayer, intermediate-intensity tissue beneath the mask that could indicate partial volume effects or fatty muscle infiltration, and I'm trying to match this against the diagonal bright band visible in the clean reference image.

The mask seems to only cover the upper part of this bright region, while the clean image shows the tissue tapering further down near the hip—possibly into muscle like the vastus intermedius. Since I can't pin down exact coordinates this way, I think I should switch to viewing a sagittal slice through the lesion's extent to get a clearer sense of its superior-inferior boundaries.

content.text: sheet sagittal 80–140/206 (8 slices) | v2 | tool calls 10/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I notice the sagittal sheet images look unusual - they seem to orient with anterior on the left and superior at top, and the lesion appears to occupy much of the slice height. I'm trying to make sense of the orientation and extent before drawing conclusions.

Looking at sagittal slices 89-140, the mask shape varies - some show a superior protrusion, others a thin horizontal strip that likely marks a medial or lateral edge. Overall the mask seems reasonable, but I want to check the gray tissue region near axial slice 128, which may require switching to a coronal view through that same anatomical position to resolve the ambiguity.

Working out the coronal-to-axial coordinate mapping, I figure the coronal index relates to the pixel row by inverting it against the image scale, giving me coronal index ≈ 206 minus the scaled y-value. Applying this to the marked point and the mask boundaries at axial 128 gives me a coronal range to check, so I'll pull up coronal slice 110 with the outline overlaid to verify.

content.text: coronal 108/206 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 11/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm checking coronal slice 108 where the lesion looks well segmented, converting the superior boundary coordinate to its corresponding axial slice, and confirming the tissue above the mask still looks like normal muscle. Now I'm examining a gray region near axial slice 128 to see if it's being captured correctly.

The intermediate-intensity region at axial 128 is ambiguous — it could be muscle with fat partial-voluming or an edge of the lesion itself. At slice 120 the mask covers the bright region fully with a tail toward the femur, while at 130 the posterior boundary is cut straight with gray tissue left uncovered below, so I want to zoom into axial 132 around the mask to judge this more carefully.

content.text: coronal 100/206 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 12/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: I'm checking whether the lesion boundaries in the clean image at coronal slice 100 line up with the corresponding mask coordinates after accounting for the panel offset, comparing both the upper lesion region and the lower right lobe extent.

content.text: coronal 100/206 | crop marks | marks fine | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 13/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm comparing the mask boundary against the clean image's lesion edge at several vertical positions, checking how far the bright region extends in x compared to where the mask cuts off.

Given the zoom scale (roughly 7.5 px/voxel), this discrepancy looks like a moderate 3-7 voxel undersegmentation on the periphery, possibly where lesion blends with adjacent muscle tissue. I think I should check the corresponding axial slices instead, since the coronal zoom crop's exact correspondence to axial slice numbers is unclear—axial 40 and 50 appeared well segmented with just a small bump, so let me examine axial 45 cropped around the mask region for more detail.

content.text: axial 40/166 | crop mask | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 14/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: The axial 40 mask fits well, so now I'm trying to pinpoint where the coronal view shows a miss, converting the coronal y-coordinates to axial slice levels to narrow down the under-segmented lateral region to around slices 20-32.

content.text: axial 24/166 | crop mask | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 15/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Comparing the lesion boundaries at axial slice 24 between the clean image and mask, I'm checking pixel offsets on the right side of the patient and finding the mask edge is slightly under by about 15 pixels, roughly 2 voxels, which is a close match given the scale.

There's also a faint grayish halo around the lesion that could be the capsule or a fat-muscle partial volume effect, which seems negligible for boundary accuracy. The real question now is the superior and inferior extent of the lesion—around axial slices 125-137 at the top and 4-15 at the bottom—so I want to look at axial 10 more closely since it showed a hazy region anterior to the mask.

content.text: axial 11/166 | crop mask | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 16/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking at axial slice 11, I'm comparing the lesion's actual clean edges against the mask boundaries — the left, right, and bottom edges roughly align with the mask, but there's a hazy anterior extension near the top that the mask doesn't fully capture.

That gray haze is likely partial volume from the lesion's tapering inferior tip, since lesions often curve obliquely in coronal/sagittal views. I want to cross-check this against sagittal 115 to see how the lesion's inferior end looks there, which should clarify whether this haze is truly part of the lesion.

content.text: sagittal 112/206 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 17/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
This sagittal view's orientation seems off, so I'm recalculating the mask boundaries — converting pixel coordinates to voxel scale to estimate the lesion's anterior-posterior extent, getting roughly 99 voxels wide.

This matches the axial view's measurement of ~107 voxels A-P, so the lesion is consistently large: around 100mm AP, 45mm wide, 130mm long. Checking the sagittal slice at 112, the mask boundary tracks the clean image's lesion edges well at both the anterior-superior region and the bottom curve, and the bright area at the anterior-superior corner is just subcutaneous fat, not lesion tissue, which the mask correctly excludes.

The mask overall looks solid, but I want to check the superior-posterior region more carefully — there's a possible protrusion visible in sagittal slice 131 and some gray area posterior to the mask in axial 128, so I should pull up axial 132 for a fuller look.

content.text: axial 124/166 | crop mask | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 18/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking at axial slice 124, the mask covers the bright lesion, but I notice a lighter-gray zone to the right of the lower half and a bright region extending posteriorly near the femur that could be fat around the femoral neck or intermuscular fat.

The medium-gray band between the mask and dark muscle could reflect partial volume effects from the lesion's oblique boundary tapering superiorly, but it's not a clear case for inclusion. I think the current mask is reasonably good, but C3 (the 27 mL candidate touching the mask on multiple sides) is substantial enough that I should check whether it captures the gray periphery at the superior end — looking at the slivers and bulges visible across axial, sagittal, and coronal views.

I don't think dilation is warranted here, since lipoma boundaries like this are typically drawn right at the fat edge, and axial 40 already looked accurate on the border. I want to pull up sagittal 131 fully to check the superior protrusion shape alongside sagittal 89.

content.text: sagittal 131/206 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 19/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Checking slice 131, the mask's protrusion boundary at top roughly matches the clean image's bright region, extending slightly further but close enough. The notch region also aligns with a dark septum band in the clean scan, so that checks out fine.

Overall the mask looks solid, but there's a possible hazy inferior tip around axial 11 anteriorly that I want to trace back to the right sagittal slice — maybe near 97-112 where the lesion bottom edge might extend past the mask. I'll pull up sagittal 100 in full to verify the inferior boundary there.

content.text: sagittal 98/206 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 20/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking at sagittal slice 98, the mask covers the main bright lesion, and below it I see gray intermediate tissue that looks like striated muscle, likely the vastus intermedius — darker than the lesion itself, with a lighter-gray patch anterior to it that's probably also muscle curving around the lesion.

The mid-gray tissue below the lesion is brighter than the pure muscle further over, which makes sense since this slice is near the lateral edge of the lesion and the mask here is smaller than at slice 112 — partial volume averaging at the margin explains the gray appearance. I'm satisfied the mask looks correct, so I'll move on to running seg_finish for the review.

arguments.reason: Well-defined fatty intramuscular mass in anterior thigh; mask follows the fat-muscle boundary in all three planes.

content.text:
Final review of v2: volume 361.0 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 4–137, coronal 70–182, sagittal 80–142 | tool calls 21/40, prompts 1/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates (second image): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong).
C1 add 90 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly anterior of the mask
C2 add 37 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly anterior of the mask
C3 add 27 mL, touches mask on its right, inferior and anterior sides, mostly superior of the mask
C4 add 9.4 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly superior of the mask
C5 add 8.1 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly posterior of the mask
candidate image: one row per candidate, columns axial / coronal / sagittal through the candidate (green outline = current mask, magenta outline + light tint = candidate; judge the tissue inside the magenta outline). For each candidate decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept) or normal tissue (reject). Accept with seg_accept and call seg_finish again for a new review; if none belong, confirm with the review code. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "5730" to save it.

content.text: case L07 finished (confidence high); final mask saved from v2 | final volume 361.0 mL, components 1 (largest 100.0%) | tool calls 22/40, prompts 1/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

I've saved the mask for case L07 and marked it high confidence. It is one connected piece of 361 mL.

**What the lesion is:** a large, bright fatty mass inside the muscle at the front of the thigh, with thin internal dividing strands. It measures about 100 mm front to back, 45 mm side to side and 130 mm top to bottom (axial slices 4–137).

**How I built the mask:**
- One model prompt (two positive points inside the mass on axial slice 83) captured the whole lesion in one go.
- I then filled small internal holes left by the dark strands, which added 0.5 mL.
- I checked the outline on axial, coronal and sagittal slices across the full length. It follows the edge between fat and muscle well, and the review slices just past each end show no remaining lesion.

**Places where the edge is slightly uncertain:**
- Over a few slices near the bottom end (around axial 20–32) the mask may sit 1–2 mm inside the lesion edge on one side.
- At both tips the lesion fades into grey, blurred tissue: in front of the lower tip (around axial 11) and next to the narrowing upper part (around axial 124–130). I left this out because it looks like edge blurring or muscle rather than definite fat.

**Automatic suggestions I rejected (5 total):**
- Four were fat under the skin or between muscles that doesn't touch the mass.
- One was a 27 mL scatter of thin slivers around the mask's edge, mostly at the top end, where I couldn't see clear lesion tissue.

I used 22 of 40 tool calls and 1 of 15 model prompts.
